title: All-optical thin-film lithium niobate memristor
abstract: Photonic memristors are essential components for neuromorphic optical computing, but their integration with optical waveguide platforms currently relies on complex fabrication procedures with high manufacturing costs. Here we show that thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN), a widely adopted photonic platform, can be transformed into an all-optically controlled memristive material, enabling the direct fabrication of photonic memristors on TFLN without the need for heterogeneous integration. Through a complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor-compatible oxygen-ion implantation process, spatially separated oxygen-doped and defect-rich layers are formed in TFLN, enabling all-optically controlled refractive index modulation. The resulting oxygen-implanted devices exhibit 3-bit multilevel non-volatile memory, ultralow switching energy of hundreds of femtojoules per bit, submicrosecond optical response and long data retention over extended operation. Wafer-scale production of TFLN and complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor-compatible ion implantation thus provide a homogeneous, scalable and programmable material platform for integrated photonic circuits and systems, with the potential for future large-scale photonic neural networks.
